intro: Covers past simple and present perfect with ago, last, yesterday, already, just, yet

items.q: I ___ my keys. I can't find them anywhere!
items.why: No time given; result relevant now — present perfect.

items.q: We ___ the report yet. We'll finish it tomorrow.
He ___ just arrived at the station, so he's still there.
items.why: 'Just' with a current result uses present perfect.
'Last Friday' is a finished past time — past simple.

parts.title: Complete the sentences with the correct form.

items.why: 'Already' with a result felt now — present perfect.
'Ago' marks a finished past moment — past simple.
'Last week' is a specific past time — past simple.
'Just' describing a very recent action — present perfect.

items.post: me yesterday, so I was worried.
items.why: 'Yesterday' is a finished time — past simple negative.

parts.title: Find and correct the mistake in each sentence.

items.sentence: I have seen that doctor last Monday.
items.corrected: I saw that doctor last Monday.
items.why: 'Last Monday' is a specific past time; past simple required.
'Yet' in negatives uses present perfect, not past simple.

items.sentence: We already finished the homework an hour ago.
items.corrected: We finished the homework an hour ago.
items.why: 'Ago' needs past simple; drop 'already' or change tense.

parts.title: Write your own sentences.
parts.pointsLabel: 2 points: 1 for correct form, 1 for meaning and use

items.prompt: Write one sentence about something you have already done today.
items.criteria: Present perfect with 'already'; no specific clock time needed.
items.example: I have already cleaned my room this morning.

items.prompt: Write one sentence about something you did yesterday evening.
items.criteria: Past simple with 'yesterday'; a clear completed action in the past.
items.example: I watched a documentary about nature yesterday evening.
